record.paper_title: Generalized Derivations and C*-Algebras: Comments and Some Open Problems
record.original_question: Let H be a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, let L(H) be the algebra of all bounded linear operators on H, and let f be a linear functional on L(H). Define alpha(f) to be the set of all pairs (A, B) in L(H) x L(H) such that f(AX) = f(XB) for every X in L(H). Characterize the conditions under which alpha(f), with the natural pair operations and adjoint inherited from L(H) x L(H), is a C*-algebra.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H$ be a separable infinite-dimensional complex Hilbert space, and let $L(H)$ denote the C*-algebra of all bounded linear operators on $H$. For a linear functional $f$ on $L(H)$, define
$$\alpha(f) = \{(A,B) \in L(H)\times L(H) : f(AX) = f(XB) \text{ for every } X \in L(H)\}.$$
Equip $L(H)\times L(H)$ with coordinatewise addition and multiplication, the natural scalar multiplication, the involution $(A,B)^* = (A^*, B^*)$, and the norm $\|(A,B)\| = \max(\|A\|,\|B\|)$ (so $L(H)\times L(H)$ becomes a C*-algebra).

(a) Determine necessary and sufficient conditions on the linear functional $f$ under which $\alpha(f)$ is a C*-subalgebra of $L(H)\times L(H)$.

(b) Equivalently, characterize those pairs $(A,B) \in L(H)\times L(H)$ that can belong to $\alpha(f)$ for some linear functional $f$ in a way that ensures $\alpha(f)$ has the structure of a C*-algebra.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a published characterization of when the set $\alpha(f)$ forms a C*-algebra. Related works on generalized derivations of C*-algebras exist, but none directly resolve this specific question. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.snippet: Discusses strongly generalized derivations from C*-algebras into Banach bimodules but does not address the alpha(f) characterization.
status_evidence.claim: Related framework, but does not resolve the alpha(f) question.

status_evidence.snippet: Studies equivalence among different definitions of generalized derivations on C*-algebras.
